Pick an audio or video file to transcribe locally (mp3, wav, mp4, mkv, and most other common formats). The file is processed on this machine and never leaves it unless you pick a cloud Engine below.

Which transcription engine to use. Offline engines (Faster-Whisper, whisper.cpp, NVIDIA Parakeet) run entirely on this machine; the two cloud engines upload your audio to Google. Set up keys/models for each in Advanced settings.

ENGINE SUMMARY
Checks this computer's NVIDIA GPU (and its memory) or CPU and RAM and suggests the fastest and the most accurate model that fit.

Which Whisper model size the Faster-Whisper engine loads — bigger models are more accurate but slower and use more RAM/VRAM. Not used by the cloud engines or NVIDIA Parakeet, which have their own model. Same picker as 'Whisper model' in Advanced settings.
Spoken language in the file. Auto detects it from the first few seconds of audio; picking it explicitly is faster and can be more accurate for short or noisy clips.
Splits the transcript by who is speaking (SPEAKER_00, SPEAKER_01, ...). Adds processing time and needs the optional sherpa-onnx component to be installed.
Force the detector to find exactly this many people, or leave on Auto.
Stores a start/end time for every individual word instead of only per sentence. Useful for karaoke-style captions or precise editing; makes the output file larger.

For a recording that switches between two languages, such as a class or an interview. Pick the first language in Language above (not Auto) and the second one here: each stretch is then written in whichever of the two it sounds like, instead of translated into one of them. Works with the faster-whisper engine, not with English translation.
Transcribe only this portion of the file (format H:MM:SS). Leave both at 0:00:00 to transcribe the whole file.
Writes English text straight from the speech in one pass, using Whisper's own translate task (no extra AI model). Output files get an .en-translated name. Works with multilingual models only.
The output files from the most recently finished transcription, with quick Open/Reveal actions. Stays empty until a job completes; see the Transcription Queue tab for jobs in progress.
Open the Hardware wizard for accelerator details.

queue: Queue is empty.  Go to the Transcribe tab and pick a file to add one.

Every transcription job you start is tracked here. Use the buttons below the list (or right-click a row) to pause, resume, cancel, re-run, or remove it; double-click a finished row to open its output folder. Speed: 4.8x means 4.8 seconds of audio were transcribed per second of work; below 1x is slower than the recording plays. The time left is a rough estimate.
download: use my browser's log-in — for Instagram, Facebook, TikTok stories, age-gated videos
format H:MM:SS — e.g. 0:00:51 to 0:01:25; leave at 0:00:00 for full video
Download all parts of this series (SMTV)
Enter a URL to load available formats
(Pause stops the download but keeps the partial file; Resume continues it)
Paste a link from YouTube or any other yt-dlp-supported site. Available formats and subtitles are looked up automatically as soon as you paste it.

Pick the browser you are logged in with. The download then uses that browser's log-in session, so videos that need an account (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok stories, age-restricted YouTube) work. The cookies are read on this computer only; nothing is uploaded. On Windows, close Chrome/Edge completely if it says it could not copy the cookie database. Same setting as Advanced › Downloads.
Where the downloaded file is saved. Defaults to the folder you last used; Browse to change it.
'Audio and video' downloads a normal video file. 'Audio' extracts just the audio track — smaller and faster if you only need the sound or plan to transcribe it.
Audio-only quality/codec choice, filled in once the URL is looked up. Higher bitrate means a larger file and better quality.
Video quality/resolution choice, filled in once the URL is looked up. Only used in 'Audio and video' mode.
Container format for the saved file (e.g. mp4). Changing it may re-encode the file instead of just repackaging it, which takes longer.
Download (and optionally transcribe) only this portion of the video instead of the whole thing. Leave both at 0:00:00 for the full length.
Downloads the video's existing subtitles/captions (auto-generated or manual) in the chosen language, instead of transcribing the audio yourself. Only available when the site provides them.
Automatically queues the downloaded file for transcription as soon as the download finishes, using the settings in the Transcribe tab.

Downloads the video, transcribes it with the Transcribe tab's settings, then burns the subtitles into a new file named <title>-subbed.mp4 next to the download. The download and the transcript files are kept. Needs 'Audio and video'.
This episode has multiple parts on the source site. Checking this queues every part, not just the one you pasted.

YouTube downloads need a small JavaScript engine (Deno, one-time download of about 40 MB from its official GitHub page, checked against its published checksum). Without it some or all YouTube formats are missing and downloads can fail.
server: Turn this on to open a simple web page that uses this app to transcribe. Open it in a browser on this computer, or share it with phones and other PCs on your network. It stays off until you start it, and there is nothing to install on the other devices.
(the number after the address; leave the default if unsure)
Share on local network (other devices can use it)

Off: only this computer can use it (no firewall prompt).
On: Windows may ask to allow it through the firewall — click Allow. Anyone on your network will be able to use it.

Leave blank for no password. If you set one, share it with the people you want to let in: they type it into the page's password box, or open the address with  ?token=YOURPASSWORD  added (letters and digits only; the page then removes it from the address bar).
Off by default. When on, the address starts with https:// and the browser will warn that the certificate is not trusted the first time — that is expected; accept it once.
Leave blank for none. When set, the server POSTs a small JSON summary to this URL each time a job finishes (or fails). Loopback and private cloud-metadata addresses are refused.

Use this only on a network you trust (your home or office Wi-Fi). It has no accounts, and unless you turn on HTTPS above it is not encrypted — anyone who can reach the address (and knows the password, if you set one) can use it. The first time you turn it on it may need to download the speech model; jobs will wait for that.
Port, network sharing, and an optional access password for the web page this tab starts. Each field also has its own note below it.

Uses its own copy of the speech model while listening, separate from the Transcribe queue.

Choose what to listen to. 'Microphone' captures an input device; 'System audio' captures whatever is currently playing on this computer — useful for a meeting, a video, or a call you are listening to.
Naming the language is more reliable than auto-detect for live audio: each chunk is short, and detection on a few seconds of speech can guess wrong and switch mid-session.

Live text only keeps up if the model transcribes faster than you speak. Tiny (the default) keeps up on any computer; bigger models are more accurate but several times too slow on a computer without a supported graphics card. Models already on this computer are shown in bold; greyed ones still need a one-time download -- use the Download button next to the picker.
Off: the session's audio recording is deleted when you stop (it takes 100-350 MB per hour). On: it is kept, and the log says where the file is.

Live audio level while listening. The waves move with the sound coming in; the bar underneath is a peak meter (green = normal speech, yellow = loud, red = close to clipping) with the level in dB at the top right. When nothing moves, nothing is being captured.
Text appears a few seconds behind the speech: the app waits for a natural pause before transcribing, so words are not cut in half.
